name: Quota-conditioned compensation and family-support pressure

attribution.legal_posture: A former-worker qualitative account describing reported compensation; it offers a team-specific account rather than an adjudicated or representative estimate for DPRK IT-worker teams.

caveats: Monitoring, communications behavior, quota pressure, subcontracting, trading activity, geography, language, and any single signal require corroboration before supporting identity, nationality, sanctions, or misconduct attribution.
Evidence and method class: source-attributed former-worker qualitative testimony.
Fraudulent employment, general DPRK overseas labor, sanctions evasion, and malicious cyber activity remain analytically distinct unless a cited source expressly connects them.
Publish only as review-level, qualitative labor-coercion context; compensation percentages remain outside the record, and pay formulas require source-specific evidence.
The compensation and family-remittance mechanism is based principally on one former-worker account; applying it to every team or dispatching organization requires broader evidence.
The report's broader survey concerned cybercrime impacts rather than IT-worker labor conditions; workforce prevalence requires labor-specific evidence.
The source mixes IT-worker, cyber-operator, and cyber-victim analysis; only the expressly IT-worker interview passages are retained here.
This record is policy, labor-governance, economic, or sanctions-evasion context; person, organization, victim, account, transaction, and incident profiles require separate records.

infrastructure.statement: One former-worker account described allowance as contingent on meeting a government-set earnings quota and linked quota success to whether money could be sent to family. Other interview material described client-driven night work, daytime development, sleep disruption, and stress when assignments did not succeed. The material supports a coercion mechanism in which compensation, family support, and work intensity are tied to performance demands.
sampling_limitations: The compensation and family-remittance mechanism is based principally on one former-worker account and cannot be generalized to every team or dispatching organization.
The report's broader survey concerned cybercrime impacts rather than IT-worker labor conditions and does not validate workforce prevalence.
The source mixes IT-worker, cyber-operator, and cyber-victim analysis; only the expressly IT-worker interview passages are retained here.
